why: The rule exists for the half-done .env.example, which is worse than its absence because it looks complete. But a repository that reads no variable at all owes nobody a .env.example: demanding it would create an empty ceremonial file in every project. The `pass` side has real code and zero `process.env`, and has to come out N/A. The `fail` side reads `API_TOKEN` and does not have the file, so the guard cannot have become an escape hatch for the whole rule.
